title: Telling what has happened
title_target: 你去过中国吗 — Nǐ qù guo Zhōngguó ma
goal: Master 了 and 过 — the two little words most often mistaken for a "past tense", which neither of them is — and negate events with 没, not 不.
bekal: tell completion 了 from change 了
negate with 没有 and know when 了 must go

dialogs.title: 对话 1 — Where did you go yesterday?
dialogs.intro: Monday morning. Wang Li asks about Andi's weekend. Notice that the verbs don't change form at all — the time is marked by time expressions, not by the verb.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: What did you do on the weekend?
lines.literal: week-end — you — do — what — (done).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: I went to the Great Wall.
lines.literal: I — go — long-wall — (done).

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: Really? Who did you go with?
lines.literal: true — (of). you — with — who — together — go — (of).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [跟|Gēn][李明|Lǐ Míng]。[我们|Wǒmen][早上|zǎoshang][六|liù][点|diǎn][就|jiù][出发|chūfā][了|le]。
lines.id: With Li Ming. We set off at six in the morning.
lines.literal: with — Li Ming. we — morning — six — o'clock — already — set-off — (done).

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: That early! Was it crowded?
lines.literal: that — early. people — many — (question).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [很|Hěn][多|duō]。[我们|Wǒmen][爬|pá][了|le][三|sān][个|ge][小时|xiǎoshí]。[太|Tài][累|lèi][了|le]！
lines.id: Very. We climbed for three hours. I was exhausted!
lines.literal: (prop) — many. we — climb — (done) — three — (classifier) — hour. too — tired — (change).

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: Did you have lunch?
lines.literal: you-all — eat — noon-meal — (done) — (question).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [没有|Méiyǒu]。[我们|Wǒmen][只|zhǐ][吃|chī][了|le][一|yí][点儿|diǎnr][面包|miànbāo]。
lines.id: No. We just had a bit of bread.
lines.literal: not-have. we — only — eat — (done) — one — bit — bread.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: Had you been to the Great Wall before?
lines.literal: you — before — go — (ever) — long-wall — (question).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: Never. This was my first time.
lines.literal: not — go — (ever). this — be — number-one — time.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.id: How was it? Worth it?
lines.literal: how. worth — (question).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [非常|Fēicháng][值得|zhíde]！[我|Wǒ][拍|pāi][了|le][两百|liǎngbǎi][多|duō][张|zhāng][照片|zhàopiàn]。
lines.id: Totally worth it! I took over two hundred photos.
lines.literal: very — worth. I — snap — (done) — two-hundred — more — (classifier) — photo.

notes: **⚠️ 了 is NOT a past-tense marker.** The sentence [我明天去了公司就回家|Wǒ míngtiān qù le gōngsī jiù huí jiā] is about **tomorrow**, and it still uses 了. What 了 marks is the **completion** of an action or a **change** of state — whenever that happens.

**So how does Mandarin mark the past? With time expressions.** [昨天|zuótiān], [上个星期|shàng ge xīngqī], [去年|qùnián], [以前|yǐqián]. The verb itself never changes — and that's the best news a Mandarin learner can get.

**⚠️ To negate an event, use [没有|méiyǒu] or [没|méi], and 了 DISAPPEARS.** [我吃了|Wǒ chī le] I've eaten → [我没吃|Wǒ méi chī] I haven't eaten. Not 我没吃了. Almost every beginner makes this mistake over and over.

**[过|guo] expresses experience: have ever, at some point in life.** [我去过中国|Wǒ qù guo Zhōngguó] I've been to China. The negative is [没去过|méi qù guo] have never been. ⚠️ Note: 过 here is read lightly, with no tone.
**了 vs 过 in one sentence:** [我去了中国|Wǒ qù le Zhōngguó] = I went to China (and may still be there). [我去过中国|Wǒ qù guo Zhōngguó] = I've been to China (I'm back; only the experience remains).

**[是…的|shì… de] highlights a detail of something that definitely happened.** [你跟谁一起去的|Nǐ gēn shéi yìqǐ qù de]？ asks **who with** — not whether you went. You'll hear this form constantly; recognize the pattern for now.
**Duration stands AFTER the verb.** [我们爬了三个小时|Wǒmen pá le sān ge xiǎoshí] we climbed for three hours. ⚠️ Don't confuse it with **when**, which stands before the verb.
**[第一次|dì-yī cì] = the first time.** [第|dì] turns a number into an ordinal: [第二|dì-èr] second, [第三|dì-sān] third.

grammars.title: The two jobs of 了
body: Mandarin has two different 了s, written with the same character. What tells them apart is **where they stand**.

head: Completion 了
Change 了
rows: At the end of the sentence
The situation has **changed** — it wasn't so before, it is now
[我买了一本书|Wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū]。
[他喝了三杯咖啡|Tā hē le sān bēi kāfēi]。
[我饿了|Wǒ è le]。 I'm hungry now.
[我看了那个电影|Wǒ kàn le nàge diànyǐng]。
[他退休了|Tā tuìxiū le]。 He's retired.

head: Sentence
Meaning
rows: I've eaten. — the state changed from hungry to full
I ate (and I'm moving on to the next thing)
[我吃了三碗饭|Wǒ chī le sān wǎn fàn]。
I ate three bowls of rice. — clear quantity, completion 了
I'm not eating after all. — change 了; note 不, not 没
Too expensive! — 了 here is part of the 太…了 pattern

after: ⚠️ **Don't stick 了 on every past sentence.** Sentences about past habits, states or background **take no 了** at all: [我小时候住在雅加达|Wǒ xiǎo shíhou zhù zài Yǎjiādá] "as a child I lived in Jakarta". No 了 there, and the sentence is still about the past.
A handy rule: **if the sentence reports a completed event — something you could follow with "and then…" — 了 is probably right.** If it describes a habit, a state or a background, leave it out.

grammars.title: 不 and 没 — two negatives

head: [不|bù]
[没|méi]
rows: Events that **haven't happened or didn't happen**
[我不喝酒|Wǒ bù hē jiǔ]。 I don't drink alcohol.
[我没喝酒|Wǒ méi hē jiǔ]。 I didn't (haven't) drink alcohol.
Yesterday I just happened not to
[不…了|bù… le] not anymore, not after all
⚠️ 没 and 了 can't go together

after: Three rules settle most doubts: **有 always takes 没有. 是 always takes 不是. An event that didn't happen always takes 没.**
⚠️ [我没去了|Wǒ méi qù le] is wrong in any form. The correct one is [我没去|Wǒ méi qù].

dialogs.title: 对话 2 — Experiences
dialogs.intro: Li Ming asks about Andi's experiences in China. Notice how 过 and 了 take turns in the same conversation.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.id: How long have you been in China?
lines.literal: you — come — China — how — long — (change).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: Three months now. Time really flies.
lines.literal: three — (classifier) — month — (change). time — pass — (marker) — really — fast.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.id: Have you ever had Peking duck?
lines.literal: you — eat — (ever) — Beijing — roast-duck — (question).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [吃|Chī][过|guo][一|yí][次|cì]。[上|Shàng][个|ge][月|yuè][跟|gēn][同事|tóngshì][一起|yìqǐ][去|qù][的|de]。
lines.id: Once. I went last month with some coworkers.
lines.literal: eat — (ever) — one — time. above — (classifier) — month — with — coworker — together — go — (of).

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.id: Was it good?
lines.literal: good-to-eat — (question).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [很|Hěn][好吃|hǎochī]，[但是|dànshì][有点儿|yǒudiǎnr][油|yóu]。[我|Wǒ][吃|chī][了|le][半|bàn][只|zhī][就|jiù][饱|bǎo][了|le]。
lines.id: Delicious, but a bit greasy. I was full after just half a duck.
lines.literal: (prop) — good-to-eat, but — have-a-bit — oily. I — eat — (done) — half — (classifier) — already — full — (change).

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.id: Have you ever taken the high-speed train?
lines.literal: you — sit — (ever) — high-rail — (question).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [还|Hái][没有|méiyǒu]。[但是|Dànshì][下|xià][个|ge][月|yuè][我|wǒ][要|yào][去|qù][上海|Shànghǎi]。
lines.id: Not yet. But next month I'm going to Shanghai.
lines.literal: still — not-have. but — below — (classifier) — month — I — will — go — Shanghai.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [那|Nà][你|nǐ][一定|yídìng][要|yào][坐|zuò][高铁|gāotiě]！[五|Wǔ][个|ge][小时|xiǎoshí][就|jiù][到|dào][了|le]。
lines.id: Then you have to take the high-speed train! You'll be there in just five hours.
lines.literal: that — you — definitely — must — sit — high-rail. five — (classifier) — hour — already — arrive — (change).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: Are the tickets expensive? I haven't bought one yet.
lines.literal: ticket — expensive — (question). I — still — not — buy — ticket.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [不|Bù][便宜|piányi]，[但是|dànshì][值得|zhíde]。[我|Wǒ][帮|bāng][你|nǐ][订|dìng][吧|ba]。
lines.id: Not cheap, but worth it. Let me book it for you.
lines.literal: not — cheap, but — worth. I — help — you — book — (suggestion).

notes: **[多久了|duō jiǔ le]？ = "how long has it been?"** The final 了 marks that the situation continues up to now. The answer uses 了 too: [三个月了|Sān ge yuè le] three months now.
**⚠️ Fourth-tone [过|guò] means "pass"; toneless [过|guo] is the experience marker.** Same character. [时间过得真快|Shíjiān guò de zhēn kuài] uses the first; [吃过|chī guo] uses the second.
**[还没有|hái méiyǒu] = "not yet".** Much softer than plain [没有|méiyǒu], because 还 implies "but maybe later". For questions like "are you married?" or "have you been there?", this is the natural answer.

**[就|jiù] signals "only … and already …"** — sooner, less or easier than expected. [吃了半只就饱了|chī le bàn zhī jiù bǎo le] full after only half; [五个小时就到了|wǔ ge xiǎoshí jiù dào le] there in just five hours.
**[只|zhī] is the classifier for animals** — including poultry served as a dish: [半只鸭子|bàn zhī yāzi] half a duck.
**[高铁|gāotiě] = high-speed train**, short for 高速铁路 "high-speed railway". The network is the largest in the world, and riding it is something Chinese people almost always recommend to visitors.
**[值得|zhíde] = worth it.** [值得去|zhíde qù] worth visiting, [不值得|bù zhíde] not worth it.

grammars.title: Telling about events — the full frame

head: Purpose
Pattern
Example
rows: [我还没买票|Wǒ hái méi mǎi piào]。
[我没坐过高铁|Wǒ méi zuò guo gāotiě]。
[我去过两次|Wǒ qù guo liǎng cì]。

after: ⚠️ **"Have you eaten?" in China often isn't a real question** — it's a greeting, like "how are you". Answering [吃了|Chī le]。 is enough, and it doesn't mean you're turning down a meal.

blocks.text: Because Mandarin verbs never change form, the whole job of marking time falls on the words below. Master them and you've mastered how Mandarin tells a story.

head: Mandarin
Meaning
Example
rows: [昨天我去了公园|Zuótiān wǒ qù le gōngyuán]。
[上个星期我很忙|Shàng ge xīngqī wǒ hěn máng]。
[上个月我去了上海|Shàng ge yuè wǒ qù le Shànghǎi]。
[去年我开始学中文|Qùnián wǒ kāishǐ xué Zhōngwén]。
[以前我不喜欢辣的|Yǐqián wǒ bù xǐhuan là de]。
[小时候我住在雅加达|Xiǎo shíhou wǒ zhù zài Yǎjiādá]。
[后来他去了美国|Hòulái tā qù le Měiguó]。
[那时候我还是学生|Nà shíhou wǒ hái shì xuésheng]。

blocks.title: Building a story
items: **Start with the time:** [上个星期天|Shàng ge xīngqītiān]…
**Continue in sequence:** [先|xiān] first · [然后|ránhòu] then · [后来|hòulái] after that · [最后|zuìhòu] finally.
**End with a judgment:** [真的很有意思|Zhēn de hěn yǒu yìsi]。 or [下次我还想去|Xià cì wǒ hái xiǎng qù]。

A full example: [上个星期天我跟朋友去了长城。我们早上六点出发，爬了三个小时。后来我们在山下吃了午饭。真的很累，但是很值得|Shàng ge xīngqītiān wǒ gēn péngyou qù le Chángchéng. Wǒmen zǎoshang liù diǎn chūfā, pá le sān ge xiǎoshí. Hòulái wǒmen zài shān xià chī le wǔfàn. Zhēn de hěn lèi, dànshì hěn zhíde]。
Notice: in a story that long, 了 appears only four times — not on every verb.

blocks.title: Sentences for talking about a trip
items: [我去过…|Wǒ qù guo…] — I've been to …
[我在…住了三天|Wǒ zài… zhù le sān tiān]。 — I stayed three days in …
[那儿的风景很美|Nàr de fēngjǐng hěn měi]。 — The scenery there is beautiful.
[人太多了|Rén tài duō le]。 — Way too many people.
[值得去|Zhíde qù]。 / [不太值得|Bú tài zhíde]。 — Worth a visit. / Not really worth it.
[下次我还想去|Xià cì wǒ hái xiǎng qù]。 — Next time I'd like to go again.

exercises.prompt: Correct these sentences, then write the correct form in pīnyīn.
items: [我没去了|Wǒ méi qù le]。
